original_card.question: Can a decoder deliver the local paid mass in fewer, larger-rank children (block frame climbs instead of rank-1 to rank-3 steps)?
methods: Find one exact small decoding identity whose frame path climbs in blocks, and price its complete per-call profile.
Bound the best effective child rank achievable for one fixed support alphabet, including copies, frames and restoration.
original_card.acceptance_gate: A per-call local profile, with all copied information, frames and restoration counted, whose ceiling exceeds the selected word's by at least 5%; masked or overcomplete supports must change an assumption of the eight-term all-pairs bound. A scoped local result may be retained without a complete supplier. Expanding it into further construction rounds requires the family-level budget and obligation gate in research-family-status.md; an optimistic passing relaxation alone is not acceptance.

first_step.inspect: Read the selected word's per-call local profile, its packing ceiling and the lever table; run levers.py for the ideal budget of the lever you target.
first_step.scope: Positive control and planning budget only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Before any synthesis, write the candidate per-call local profile (and centre charge / unpaid coordinates if changed) and screen it with ceiling.ceiling(); reject it if even the ideal ceiling does not beat the selected word's by your stated margin. Ideal budget: rank-16 delivery is 2.31x (levers.py).
original_card.bottleneck_link: Rank-1 children are about half of recursive cost; the selected word's effective child rank is about 3.9. Larger-rank delivery lowers recursive cost per unit of paid mass.
allowed_variations: One masked, overcomplete or block decoder family with exact labels and supports.
A scoped lower bound on effective rank for one alphabet.
If the coverage law, template or guard changes, derive an applicable fully charged replacement bound instead of applying the incumbent ceiling outside its scope.
scope_change_triggers: Repacking idle remainders of an unchanged word (covered by the packing ceiling).
Repeating the eight-term all-pairs search inside its proved scope.
Only changing helper terminal subspaces and monotone frames within the fixed scalar word, entrances and cleanup contract already covered by #1995/#2013.

Searching below C=40 in the #2017 Eisenstein binary scalar-rectangle or fixed-support block-linear additive pairing model; specify a changed premise instead. This bound does not cover every complex decoder.

Continuing a partial cost improvement while leaving the same unpriced consumer, restoration or central-readout obligation unresolved; refresh the family expansion decision first. Local product-retiming evidence has a narrow scope and is not a ban on changed graphs or contracts.

actual_scope: Screen the selected complex source for direct fusion of successive rank-one frame climbs into an available rank-two endpoint recipe, including exact scalar-interference windows in both orientations.
scope_change_reason: The task card asks for a new block decoder and fully charged profile. This first experiment is a bounded source-level feasibility screen for the attachment's two-level macro-fusion idea; it does not synthesize a decoder or claim a profile improvement.
bottleneck_link: The selected complex word contains 2,412 rank-one children, and the recursive cost is concave in child rank when a > 0. An exact two-rank-one to one-rank-two replacement would lower that pair's recursive charge by a factor 2^-a, but only if the composed operator and all intervening work are preserved.
stop_rule: Stop the direct-replacement screen when every selected-source rank-one successor pair has been checked against exact rank-two endpoint recipes in both orientations. Do not claim macro equivalence from matching endpoint frames. Continue only by reconstructing one candidate's complete operator and scalar window, then charging its full joint realization.
evidence: Both orientations contain 2,412 rank-one climbs, 1,441 successive rank-one climb links per register history, and 35 pairs with an available rank-two recipe on the combined endpoint frames. Every candidate is interrupted by same-register scalar operations (histogram: 10 with one touch, 5 with two, and 20 with five); there are zero direct substitutions preserving the existing schedule. Across 100 candidate/add-operand instances, no source register receives the exact same rank-one frame transition anywhere in the trace, so the simplest linearity-based reuse route is absent. This is a scoped negative screen, not a proof against redesigned macrocircuits; no exact composition equality, new supplier, or kappa improvement is claimed.

open_questions.question: Can a changed-basis or multi-operation rank-two macro absorb one of the minimally interrupted candidate pairs while preserving the exact selected operator and lowering the complete recursive profile cost?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Direct substitution fails for all candidates, and no candidate's add operand already receives the same rank-one transition. A successful joint macro must therefore synthesize the scalar window and find a new equivalent call structure rather than merely reuse an existing climb.
open_questions.first_step: Start with the forward phase-B candidate on register 195: event indices 12806 and 13402 climb 0→2→252, with the sole same-register touch `add L195, L521`. Reconstruct the complete intervening region and both child maps, compare its joint operator with the pinned direct rank-two recipe on a complete exact basis, then price all changed registers and restoration.
open_questions.blocked_by: The selected rank-two endpoint recipe is not an equality certificate for the composition of the two rank-one maps and scalar window. The same-key partner census is negative; equivalent calls in another basis and the surrounding-register/restoration invoice remain unexplored.
